Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

We will continue with module 6 on corrosion chemistry, and today's class we are going to talk about corrosion control.

Key details

  • In that we will look at metallic coating and specifically galvanization and tinning.
  • When we talk of corrosion control, the first thing which comes to our mind is to create a barrier between the surface and the environment.
  • So protective coating is a very good method by which we can control corrosion to a great extent.
  • In protective coating, we have metallic coating, inorganic coating, and organic coating.
  • Then another method of corrosion control is to use corrosion inhibitors.
  • Again, we have two classes here: anodic inhibitors and catodic inhibitors.
  • The other method would be cathodic protection, and in that we are going to study about two methods in there, that is sacrificial anode method and the impressed cathodic current method.
  • Finally, we will study about anodic protection, which is also known as impressed anodic current method.
  • The first type of coating we are going to look at is metallic coating.
  • Corrosion of the base metal can be prevented by coating it with a layer of another metal over it.
  • Therefore, we will have two types of coatings which are possible.
  • One is called anodic metal coating where we are going to coat a layer of metal which is anodic with respect to the base metal.
  • Which is cathodic with respect to the base metal.
  • As I said just now, the coating metal is more active with respect to the base metal.
  • Is not completely covered, it is not going to undergo pitting corrosion.
  • This is a very big advantage of anodic metal coating.
  • With another metal, say this is M2.
  • To the base metal.
  • Therefore, even if there is a gap here, we will find that if the coating is not completely covering the surface, there is a gap on the surface.
  • You have studied that.
  • This will not give rise to pitting corrosion because as long as the anode is in contact with the.
  • Cathode, it is the anode which undergoes corrosion.
  • That is the biggest advantage of having anodic metal coating.
  • When we cover the metal with zinc on the surface, like zinc is acting as the coating, then this process is known as galvanization.
  • It's usually on iron.
  • Coating a layer of zinc on iron would be referred to as galvanization.
  • What would be the various steps involved in this process?
  • Make sure that the surface is absolutely clean because we know any coating when it is made on a surface, the smoother the surface, the better the coating is going to adhere to the surface.
  • So the first and foremost treatment before.
  • coating any surface is to make it absolutely clean.
  • So in that the first step would be.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Let us start with protective coatings.
  • A good example would be if you have an iron article and you are covering it with zinc metal, this would be anodic metal coating and then there is another method where we which we call it as the cathodic metal coating where we are going to coat the metal with another metal.
  • And an example for that would be an iron article which is coated with tin.
